scenes.say: Ever wonder how to catch performance issues before users do? Let's see how profiling .NET apps reveals bottlenecks fast.

scenes.label: Profiling
scenes.sub: Measuring CPU, memory, and garbage collection to find slow spots.
scenes.say: Profiling means tracking things like CPU, memory, and garbage collection. The goal? Spot what’s slowing your app down.

scenes.title: Quick Profiling Commands
scenes.say: Use dotnet counters to watch real-time metrics, like garbage collection pauses. Dotnet trace digs into method timings for deeper analysis.
Here's my usual flow: choose a profiler, run the app under real conditions, gather metrics, then dig into the results to fix issues.

scenes.question: Is profiling just for memory leaks?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it's only for memory issues.
scenes.right: No, profiling covers CPU, memory, and more. It's key for finding all kinds of bottlenecks.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this one—profiling isn't just about memory leaks. It helps you catch slow code, garbage collection hiccups, and other performance problems.
